data.narrative:
XMOS is a growth-stage semiconductor company that has raised £200M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 peers in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including three public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and eight private companies (led by Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent).

The peer-median method is not applicable here. The narrow peer set—filtered by stage and valuation tier—yields fewer than three datapoints necessary for robust triangulation. While the broader Chips & Semiconductors universe contains 11 companies, the same-stage and adjacent-stage subsets are too sparse to support a reliable median calculation. Relying on an all-sector median would obscure meaningful differences in business model, technology maturity, and capital efficiency across the semiconductor landscape.

Given these constraints, a traditional valuation range cannot be derived from the available comp data. Any credible assessment would require either: (1) expansion beyond strict stage/tier filters to include the broader peer universe with explicit adjustment factors, or (2) supplementary methods such as revenue multiple analysis or discounted cash flow modeling using company-specific metrics. The key uncertainty is the scarcity of directly comparable growth-stage semiconductor companies in the current dataset, making cross-sectional valuation inherently limited without additional methodology or data.
